content.text: I read the release in full and checked every figure, period and basis in the brief against it.

facts.evidence: "The Firm reported net revenues of $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with $16.8 billion in the same period last year." (the "record" descriptor appears in the brief's headline)
"Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or $3.46 per diluted share, versus $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share, a year ago."
"Institutional Securities reported record net revenues of $11.0 billion" (the $7.6 billion year-ago comparator is not given)
"Return on tangible common equity (a non-GAAP measure) was 26.6%, compared with 18.2% a year ago."
"driven by a 69% increase in Equity net revenues to $6.3 billion" (the "record" descriptor is not carried over)

"Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion, supported by asset management fees on elevated assets and higher net interest income." (the 30.5% pre-tax margin is not stated anywhere in the brief)

"The business added a record $148 billion in net new assets, bringing total fee-based client assets to $3.0 trillion." (the release's qualifier that just over half of the inflows related to IPOs of certain Workplace-channel clients is omitted)
"The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.15 per share, payable on August 14, 2026." (the 15 cent increase is not mentioned)
"The Board reauthorized a multi-year common equity share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, beginning in the third quarter of 2026." (the absence of a set expiration date is not mentioned)
"The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8% at the end of the second quarter, down from 15.0% in the prior-year period."

claims.claim: Net revenues were $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Net revenues were $16.8 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion in the quarter.
Earnings per diluted share were $3.46 in the quarter.
A year ago, net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share.
Pre-tax income was $7.3 billion for the quarter.
Pre-tax income was $4.6 billion in the prior-year period.
The expense efficiency ratio was 65% for the second quarter.
The expense efficiency ratio was 65% for the first half of the year.
Return on tangible common equity, a non-GAAP measure, was 26.6% in the quarter.
Return on tangible common equity was 18.2% a year ago.
Book value per share was $67.80, up from $61.59 in the prior-year quarter.
The effective tax rate for the current quarter was 23.1%.
Institutional Securities reported record net revenues of $11.0 billion.
The Institutional Securities result was driven by the increases in Equity and Investment Banking net revenues.
Equity net revenues rose 69% to $6.3 billion.
Investment Banking net revenues rose 58% to $2.4 billion.
Fixed Income net revenues increased 13% to $2.5 billion.
Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion.
Wealth Management net revenues were supported by asset management fees on elevated assets and higher net interest income.
Wealth Management added a record $148 billion in net new assets in the quarter.
Wealth Management total fee-based client assets were $3.0 trillion.
The record net new assets brought total fee-based client assets to $3.0 trillion.
claims.note: The release reports fee-based client assets of $3,022 billion but never links that level to net new assets. They are distinct metrics: fee-based asset flows were $39.1 billion in the quarter, while net new assets were $148.1 billion, and the release attributes elevated asset management revenues to higher markets and cumulative fee-based flows.

claims.claim: Investment Management reported net revenues of $1.6 billion.
Investment Management net revenues were primarily driven by asset management fees on higher average AUM.
Investment Management AUM reached $2.0 trillion.
Investment Management had positive long-term net flows of $7.5 billion for the quarter.
The release does not provide specific financial guidance or outlook for future periods.
The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8% at the end of the second quarter.
The Standardized CET1 ratio was 15.0% in the prior-year period.
The Firm repurchased $1.5 billion of outstanding common stock during the quarter.
The Board reauthorized a multi-year common equity share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, beginning in the third quarter of 2026.
The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.15 per share, payable on August 14, 2026.
Institutional Securities reported Other net revenues of $(152) million.
The Other net revenue result was primarily due to higher mark-to-market losses on corporate loans, inclusive of hedges.
Wealth Management transactional revenues excluded mark-to-market gains on investments associated with DCP that were present in the prior year.
DCP hedges have been transitioned to derivatives, affecting compensation expense rather than net revenues.
The DCP presentation change may alter period-over-period comparability.
Provision for credit losses decreased to $98 million from $196 million a year ago.
The decrease in the provision for credit losses was driven by portfolio growth and individual assessments for corporate and commercial real estate loans.
claims.note: Misattribution. The release cites portfolio growth in corporate loans and secured lending facilities and individual assessments for certain corporate and CRE loans as drivers of the Institutional Securities provision recorded in the quarter, not as the cause of the year-over-year decline in the Firm's provision; the release gives no explanation for the decline.
